correctness.rationale: For every connected simple undirected labeled graph through six vertices, reconstruct degree, closeness (n-1)/distance sum, and unnormalized Freeman betweenness (shortest-path shares over unordered endpoint pairs). An independent complete 2^(n choose 2) graph enumeration, exact-rational shortest-path counting and canonical isomorphism reduction obtains connected counts (1,1,4,38,728,26704), unique degree/betweenness leader disagreements (0,0,0,0,0,720), tie-level set differences 150 at order five, and a single asymmetric six-vertex class of orbit 720. Its edge representative {01,03,05,12,13,14,23,24} has unique degree/closeness leader vertex 1 and betweenness leader vertex 0. Complete finite enumeration proves the bounded claim, no assertion for n>6.

evidence: The published complete-bipartite/tree betweenness formulas cover proper graph subclasses; the witness contains a cycle and does not belong to those covering families.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Broad elementary formulas and qualitative separation have no theorem enumerating all connected graphs of orders five/six; no stronger statement was found implying the census.

originality.rationale: The familiar qualitative inequivalence of degree, closeness and betweenness is classical and not new. Independent comparison considers stronger family formulas and the exact graph-isomorphism boundary: Freeman defines the measures, and Unnithan et al. calculate betweenness in paths, stars, wheels, bipartite graphs and trees without a theorem classifying the least order of distinct unique maximizers. No dominating published exact 720/26704 first-layer classification was found; this is best-of-knowledge originality, not guaranteed novelty.
residual_risks: Unindexed small-network textbooks, graph-atlas tables or theses might tabulate the same six-vertex unique-maximizer class.
Only connected, simple, undirected graphs of order at most six were exhaustively classified; rankings and larger orders excluded.

value.rationale: The first graph order at which two canonical centrality notions choose different unambiguous leaders is a motivated structural threshold. Its unique isomorphism witness and exact orbit count tell network-centrality researchers how the divergence arises, and clarifying the order-five tie case prevents a misleading threshold statement. Finite classification is a substantive completed natural census, not an arbitrary numerical sample.
